title: Weather
about: Collocations for talking about the weather: sunshine and heat, rain, fog, snow, frost and wind (heavy rain, thick fog, a biting wind), and words for extreme weather like gale-force winds and rivers bursting their banks.

parts.title: More weather collocations
parts.note: Ще кілька сполучень із вправи 13.5: їх варто знайти в словнику до слів wind, rain і snow. І запам'ятай шкалу руйнувань від слабшого до сильнішого: damage (пошкодити) → destroy (знищити будинок, міст) → devastate (спустошити цілу місцевість).

rows: a sudden short burst of strong wind
A gust of wind turned my umbrella inside out.
There wasn't a breath of wind, and the lake was as smooth as glass.
We sheltered in a shop doorway until the shower was over.
a short period of very heavy rain
A sudden downpour sent everyone at the barbecue running indoors.
snow comes down from the sky
Snow was falling softly as we walked home from the party.
By lunchtime the snow had melted, and the paths were covered in slush.

items.pattern: unbroken sunshine · days / a week of unbroken sunshine · also unbroken cloud
items.meaning: sunshine all day long, with no clouds at all
items.example: We've had a week of **unbroken sunshine**, and the garden is crying out for rain.
more: On the first day of **unbroken sunshine**, the beach was full by nine o'clock.
Our tomatoes love **unbroken sunshine**: they've grown so fast this week.
items.watchOut: Unbroken тут не «незламаний», а «без перерви». Так само кажуть про хмари: unbroken cloud — суцільна хмарність без жодного просвіту. Unbreakable — інше слово: «який не можна зламати» (unbreakable glass).

items.pattern: scorching hot · a scorching (hot) day · the scorching sun / heat · opposite: freezing cold
items.meaning: extremely hot, so hot that it almost burns
items.example: It was **scorching hot** at the bus stop, and there was no shade anywhere.
more: The sand was **scorching hot**, so we ran down to the water on tiptoe.
We spent a **scorching** afternoon in the queue for the water park.
items.watchOut: «Дуже спекотно» — не strongly hot. Кажуть very hot, boiling hot або scorching hot. Scorching звучить найсильніше: так спекотно, що аж пече.

items.pattern: soak up the sunshine / the sun · lie / sit somewhere soaking up the sun
items.meaning: enjoy lying or sitting in the sun for a long time
items.uk: ніжитися на сонці, вбирати сонячне тепло
items.example: Grandad sat on the bench outside the café, **soaking up the sunshine**.
more: After a long winter, I just want to lie in the garden and **soak up the sun**.
Lizards lie on the warm rocks, **soaking up the sun**.
items.watchOut: «Засмагати, приймати сонячні ванни» — sunbathe або soak up the sun. Take sun baths звучить як дослівний переклад: так зазвичай не кажуть.

items.pattern: it's pouring (with rain) · it's pouring down · the pouring rain
items.meaning: raining very heavily
items.uk: ллє як з відра, періщить дощ
items.example: It was **pouring with rain** when we came out of the cinema, and we had no umbrella.
more: Look outside, it's **pouring**! Have you got an umbrella I can borrow?
We stood in the **pouring rain** for an hour, waiting for the gates to open.
items.watchOut: «Ллє як з відра» — it's pouring (with rain), без відра. Ідіома raining cats and dogs існує, але в живій мові трапляється рідше, ніж у підручниках. Розмовне британське — it's chucking it down.

items.pattern: torrential rain / downpours
items.meaning: extremely heavy rain that falls hard and fast
items.example: **Torrential rain** turned the campsite into a muddy lake overnight.
more: The open-air concert stopped after ten minutes of **torrential rain**.
We got caught in **torrential rain** on the way back from the market.
items.watchOut: Torrential вживають майже лише з rain і downpour. Це сильніше, ніж heavy rain: справжня злива. Наголос на другий склад: tor-REN-tial.

items.pattern: freezing cold · also bitterly cold · it's freezing · opposite: scorching hot
items.meaning: extremely cold
items.example: The changing rooms at the pool were **freezing cold**, so we got dressed as fast as we could.
more: The milk from the fridge was **freezing cold**, so I warmed it up a bit.
Our classroom was **freezing cold** because the heating had broken down.
items.watchOut: Freezing cold — не обов'язково нижче нуля, просто «дуже холодно». Не плутай з frozen — замерзлий (a frozen lake). «Я змерз» — I'm freezing або I'm frozen.

items.pattern: get soaked (to the skin) · be soaked · soaked through
items.meaning: become completely wet
items.example: I forgot my umbrella and **got soaked** walking from the station.
more: The dog jumped into the lake and came out **soaked**.
The festival was great, even though everyone **got soaked to the skin**.
items.watchOut: «Промокнути до нитки» — get soaked to the skin, дослівно «до шкіри», а не to the thread. Можна й get wet through або get drenched.

items.pattern: a break in the clouds / the rain · also a gap in the clouds
items.meaning: a gap in the clouds where the sun comes through; in the rain, a short time when it stops
items.uk: просвіт у хмарах; перерва в дощі
items.example: At last there was **a break in the clouds**, and the whole valley lit up in the sun.
more: Let's wait for **a break in the rain** before we walk the dog.
The pilot said we'd see the Alps if there was **a break in the clouds**.
items.watchOut: Break тут не «злам», а перерва, просвіт. «Просвіт у хмарах» — a break (або a gap) in the clouds. A break in the rain — коли дощ ненадовго вщух.

items.pattern: it rains heavily / hard · rain falls heavily
items.meaning: rain falls hard and there is a lot of it
items.example: When it **rains heavily**, water comes in under our back door.
more: If it **rains heavily** tomorrow, we'll take the kids to the museum instead.
It's been **raining hard** since lunch, and the garden is like a swamp.
items.watchOut: «Сильно дощить» — it's raining heavily або it's raining hard, не strongly. Обережно: hard — сильно, а hardly — ледве: It hardly rained — дощу майже не було.

items.pattern: thick / heavy cloud · low / grey cloud · often uncountable: There's thick cloud
items.meaning: a lot of cloud that hides the sun
items.example: **Thick cloud** hid the moon, so we couldn't see the eclipse.
more: **Thick cloud** will cover most of the country tomorrow morning.
Our plane flew through **thick cloud** for twenty minutes before we saw the sea.
items.watchOut: У прогнозах cloud часто незлічуване і без a: There's thick cloud. «Хмарність» — cloud або cloud cover; слово cloudiness у розмові майже не вживають.

items.pattern: it looks like rain · it looks like / as if it's going to rain
items.meaning: the sky shows that it will probably rain soon
items.uk: схоже, буде дощ; збирається на дощ
items.example: Take your raincoat. It **looks like rain**.
more: It **looked like rain** all afternoon, but not a drop fell.
We'd better hurry home: it **looks as if it's going to rain**.
items.watchOut: Після like тут найпростіше іменник: It looks like rain. Можна й повним реченням: It looks like it's going to rain. Looks like raining у британській розмовній мові трапляється, але звучить незвично — краще rain.

items.pattern: the weather deteriorates · informal: gets worse · opposite: improves
items.meaning: the weather becomes worse
items.example: The ferry was cancelled because the weather **deteriorated** in the afternoon.
more: The weather is expected to **get worse** over the weekend.
If the weather **deteriorates**, the climbers will turn back.
items.watchOut: «Погода зіпсується» — the weather will get worse (розмовне) або deteriorate (формальніше, як у прогнозах). The weather will spoil — калька. Зате з додатком spoil працює: The rain spoilt our picnic.

items.pattern: thick / dense fog · also heavy fog · thick mist
items.meaning: fog that is so heavy you can hardly see through it
items.example: Our flight was delayed for three hours because of **thick fog**.
more: We got lost in **dense fog** on the way down the mountain.
The bridge disappeared into the **thick fog** halfway across the river.
items.watchOut: Українською туман «густий» — і англійською так само: thick або dense fog (можна й heavy fog). А от «сильний туман» — не strong fog.

items.pattern: patches of fog / mist · patchy fog
items.meaning: small areas of fog or mist here and there
items.example: Early in the morning there were **patches of mist** over the fields, like cotton wool.
more: The train slowed down every time it went through **patches of fog**.
**Patchy fog** this morning will clear by lunchtime.
items.watchOut: «Місцями туман» — patches of fog або patchy fog. Pieces of fog так не кажуть.

items.pattern: a blanket of fog / mist / snow · literary
items.meaning: a thick layer of fog or snow that covers a large area
items.example: **A blanket of fog** lay over the town, and only the church tower showed above it.
more: By Christmas morning **a blanket of snow** covered the whole village.
**A blanket of mist** hung over the lake at sunrise.
items.watchOut: Patches — невеликі ділянки туману, a blanket — суцільна густа пелена на великій території. Звучить книжно: у розмові частіше кажуть просто thick fog.

items.pattern: the fog / mist comes down · opposite: lifts
items.meaning: fog or mist appears and covers an area
items.example: The mist **came down** while we were on the beach, and we could hardly see the sea.
more: When the fog **comes down** on the mountain, the cable car stops running.
We were driving across the moor when the fog **came down**.

items.pattern: the fog / mist lifts · lift – lifted · opposite: comes down
items.meaning: fog or mist disappears and you can see clearly again
items.example: By ten o'clock the fog had **lifted**, and we could see the islands.
more: The race will start as soon as the mist **lifts**.
The morning mist **lifted** slowly, and the hills appeared one by one.
items.watchOut: «Туман розсіявся» — the fog lifted або cleared, не scattered. Rise про туман теж кажуть, але це радше «здіймається» (mist rising from the river), а не «зникає».

items.pattern: the sun is strong · strong sun · opposite: weak sun
items.meaning: sunshine that is very hot and can easily burn your skin
items.example: The sun is so **strong** here that you can burn in ten minutes.
more: My nose always burns in **strong sun**.
The **weak** winter sun was low in the sky by three o'clock.
items.watchOut: «Активне сонце» — калька: англійською the sun is strong. А от дощ strong не буває: heavy rain.

items.pattern: heavy rain (NOT strong rain) · opposite: light rain
items.meaning: a lot of rain falling
items.example: We had to stop the car because of **heavy rain**: the wipers couldn't cope.
more: **Heavy rain** is expected across the whole country on Saturday.
The forecast is for **light rain** in the morning and sunshine later.
items.watchOut: Найчастіша калька: «сильний дощ» — heavy rain, не strong rain. Так само heavy snow. А вітер — навпаки, strong wind.

items.pattern: driving rain / snow
items.meaning: rain or snow that falls fast and hard, blown by the wind
items.uk: косий дощ із вітром, дощ періщить в обличчя
items.example: The postman cycled along the seafront through the **driving rain**.
more: We put up the tent in **driving rain**, and everything got wet.
The match went on in **driving snow**, and the players could hardly see the ball.
items.watchOut: Driving тут не про водіння: дощ «жене» вітер. Тому driving rain — не просто сильний дощ, а дощ, що з вітром б'є в обличчя.

items.pattern: heavy snow (falling) · thick / deep snow (on the ground) · heavy snowfall
items.meaning: a lot of snow falling, or a deep layer of snow on the ground
items.example: **Heavy snow** fell all night, and the schools were closed in the morning.
more: The village was cut off by **thick snow** for three days.
We had to dig the car out of the **thick snow** before we could drive to work.
items.watchOut: «Сильний сніг» — heavy snow, не strong snow; «великий снігопад» — heavy snowfall, не big snow. Про сніг на землі — thick або deep snow.

items.pattern: crisp snow · also fresh snow (that has just fallen)
items.meaning: fresh, hard snow that crunches when you walk on it
items.uk: свіжий, хрусткий сніг (що рипить під ногами)
items.example: We went for a long walk in the **crisp snow** and came back with rosy cheeks.
more: Overnight there was ten centimetres of **fresh snow** on the ski slopes.
On a cold, sunny morning the snow is **crisp** and sparkles in the light.
items.watchOut: «Сніг рипить під ногами» — the snow crunches. Crisp — про свіжий твердий сніг; crispy зазвичай кажуть про їжу (crispy bacon).

items.pattern: a hard frost · opposite: a light frost (NOT a soft frost)
items.meaning: a time when it is so cold that the ground freezes hard and everything is covered in ice
items.example: A **hard frost** overnight left the car windscreen covered in thick ice.
more: We had a **hard frost** in April, and the apple blossom turned brown.
A **light frost** in the morning is nothing to worry about: it'll be gone by nine.
items.watchOut: Frost — це іній або заморозок, коли вночі мінус. «Сильний мороз (заморозок)» — a hard frost; strong frost так зазвичай не кажуть. Слабкий — a light frost, не a soft frost.

items.pattern: strong / high wind(s) · a strong wind is blowing · high winds (mostly plural, in forecasts and news)
items.meaning: very powerful wind
items.example: The bridge was closed to lorries because of **high winds**.
more: A **strong wind** blew the umbrella out of my hand.
**Strong winds** are expected along the coast tonight.
items.watchOut: Тут збігається з українською: сильний вітер — strong wind. Ще кажуть high winds (зазвичай у множині, у прогнозах і новинах). Але high, не tall: tall — про людей, дерева, будинки.

items.pattern: a light wind / light winds · opposite: strong wind
items.meaning: a gentle wind that is not strong
items.example: There was only a **light wind**, so the sailing lesson was very slow.
more: On calm days with **light winds**, we take the boat out to the island.
A **light wind** was moving the leaves: perfect weather for a picnic.
items.watchOut: «Слабкий вітер» — найчастіше a light wind або a gentle breeze. Weak wind кажуть значно рідше.

items.pattern: a biting wind · also a bitter / icy wind
items.meaning: a very cold wind that hurts your face
items.example: We stood on the platform in a **biting wind** for half an hour.
more: Put on a scarf: there's a **biting wind** down by the river.
A **biting** north **wind** made our walk along the cliffs much shorter than we'd planned.
items.watchOut: «Пронизливий, колючий вітер» — a biting wind (дослівно «кусючий»), не a prickly wind. Можна ще a bitter або an icy wind.

items.pattern: the wind picks up · picked up · opposite: dies down
items.meaning: the wind gets stronger
items.example: The wind **picked up** in the afternoon, so we packed up the picnic.
more: Let's get back to the harbour before the wind **picks up**.
As the wind **picked up**, the trees in the park began to sway.
items.watchOut: «Вітер посилився» — the wind picked up (розмовне) або got stronger. Strengthened звучить формально, як у прогнозі.

items.pattern: the wind dies down · died down · opposite: picks up
items.meaning: the wind gets weaker and then stops
items.example: We waited for the wind to **die down** before we put up the tent.
more: By midnight the wind had **died down**, and the sea was calm.
As the wind **died down**, the waves got smaller and smaller.
items.watchOut: «Вітер ущух» — the wind died down (або dropped). Died тут не «помер», а «стих». Так само кажуть про шум чи оплески: the noise died down.

items.pattern: the wind blows · the wind whistles (through / round sth) · blow – blew – blown
items.meaning: the wind moves the air; it makes a high sound when it passes through a narrow space
items.example: All night the wind **whistled** round the old farmhouse.
more: The wind was **blowing** so hard that we couldn't open the car door.
I could hear the wind **whistling** through the gap under the door.
items.watchOut: Минулий час — blew, не blowed. У whistle t не вимовляється: /ˈwɪsl/.

items.pattern: freak weather (conditions) · a freak storm / hailstorm / wave
items.meaning: very unusual and unexpected weather, often violent
items.example: A **freak hailstorm** in July flattened half the vegetable gardens in the village.
more: **Freak weather** brought snow to the beach in the middle of May.
Two boats were damaged by a **freak wave** during the storm.
items.watchOut: «Аномальна погода» — частіше freak weather (або unusual, extreme weather): anomalous weather звучить науково. Freak як прикметник — «дивний і несподіваний»: a freak accident.

items.pattern: a storm / bad weather hits / strikes a place · hit – hit – hit · strike – struck – struck
items.meaning: reach a place suddenly and affect it badly
items.example: The storm **hit** the coast just after midnight.
more: A tornado **struck** the small town without warning.
Bad weather **hit** the south-east on Friday, just as the holidays began.
items.watchOut: «Буря налетіла на місто, накрила місто» — the storm hit / struck the town. Covered і fell on тут не кажуть. Минулий час strike — struck.

items.pattern: gale-force winds · a gale · a gale warning
items.meaning: extremely strong winds
items.example: **Gale-force winds** knocked out the power to thousands of homes.
more: **Gale-force winds** made it impossible to put up the marquee for the wedding.
The lorry was blown over by **gale-force winds** on the bridge.
items.watchOut: Gale — це сам дуже сильний вітер, а storm — буря загалом (вітер, дощ, грім). «Штормове попередження» — a gale warning або a storm warning.

items.pattern: cause (a lot of / serious / minor) damage to sth · damage is uncountable
items.meaning: harm or break things
items.example: The flood **caused a lot of damage** to the shops on the high street.
more: Luckily, the storm **caused** only minor **damage** to our house: a few broken tiles.
Salt on the roads **causes** a lot of **damage** to cars in winter.
items.watchOut: «Завдати шкоди» — cause damage, не make damage і не give damage. Damage тут незлічуване: a lot of damage, без -s. Damages у множині — компенсація, яку присуджує суд.

items.pattern: devastate a town / an area · be devastated by sth
items.meaning: destroy or badly damage most of a place
items.example: The floods **devastated** the farms along the river, and many families lost everything.
more: The drought **devastated** the harvest across the whole country.
The town was **devastated** by an earthquake in 1980.
items.watchOut: Від слабшого до сильнішого: damage (пошкодити) → destroy (знищити будинок, міст) → devastate (спустошити цілу місцевість). Про людину be devastated — бути вбитим горем. Пишеться devastated, не devasted.

items.pattern: buildings / houses are destroyed · completely destroyed
items.meaning: damaged so badly that they no longer exist or can't be used
items.example: Two houses were completely **destroyed** when the river flooded.
more: Hundreds of homes were **destroyed** by the hurricane.
The bridge was **destroyed**, so the village was cut off for weeks.
items.watchOut: «Будинок зруйновано» — the house was destroyed. Broken про будинки не кажуть: broken — про вікно, чашку, ногу. Ruined — частіше «зіпсований» (a ruined holiday) або «у руїнах» (a ruined castle).

items.pattern: tear sth off · a roof is torn off · tear – tore – torn
items.meaning: pulled off violently by the wind
items.example: During the storm a huge gust **tore** the roof **off** the bus station.
more: Half the roofs in the village were **torn off** during the night.
The storm **tore** the tiles **off** the church roof.
items.watchOut: «Зірвало дах» — англійською з підметом: the wind tore the roof off, або пасив: the roof was torn off. Дієслово tear (рвати) читається /teə/, як bear, а не як tear (сльоза).

items.pattern: blow sth down · sth is blown down · blow – blew – blown
items.meaning: made to fall to the ground by the wind
items.example: Our garden fence was **blown down** in the night, and the dog ran off.
more: The wind **blew down** two old trees in the park.
The wind **blew** the children's tent **down**, so they slept indoors after all.
items.watchOut: «Вітер повалив дерево» — the wind blew the tree down або the tree was blown down. Не плутай: blow up — вибухнути, підірвати.

items.pattern: a river bursts its banks · burst – burst – burst
items.meaning: the water rises over the sides of the river and floods the land
items.example: After a week of rain, the river **burst its banks** and flooded the fields.
more: The stream at the bottom of our garden **burst its banks** last winter.
If the rain doesn't stop, the river could **burst its banks** by Friday.
items.watchOut: «Річка вийшла з берегів» — the river burst its banks, не went out of its banks. Burst не змінюється: burst – burst – burst (не bursted).

warmup.uk: Учора йшов сильний дощ, і тепер у підвалі вода.
warmup.q: There was ___ rain yesterday, and now there's water in the cellar.
warmup.explain: Сильний дощ — heavy rain. Strong rain — найчастіша калька.

warmup.uk: Не виходь без парасольки — ллє як з відра!
warmup.q: Don't go out without an umbrella: it's ___!
warmup.explain: Ллє як з відра — it's pouring (with rain). Відро англійською не потрібне.

warmup.uk: Поки ми бігли до машини, промокли до нитки.
warmup.q: We got ___ running to the car.
warmup.explain: Промокнути до нитки — get soaked to the skin, дослівно «до шкіри».

warmup.uk: Зранку був такий сильний туман, що я не бачив сусіднього будинку.
warmup.q: In the morning the fog was so ___ that I couldn't see the house next door.
warmup.explain: Сильний, густий туман — thick або dense fog, не strong fog.

warmup.uk: Синоптики попереджають про сильний заморозок уночі.
warmup.q: The forecast warns of a ___ frost tonight.
warmup.explain: Сильний заморозок — a hard frost; слабкий — a light frost (не soft).

warmup.uk: Коли вітер ущух, ми знову розпалили багаття.
warmup.q: When the wind ___, we lit the campfire again.
warmup.explain: Вітер ущух — the wind died down (або dropped). Died тут — «стих», а не «помер».

warmup.q: The wind ___ a lot of damage to the forest.
warmup.explain: Завдати шкоди — cause damage (у розмові ще do damage). Make damage — калька.

warmup.uk: Навесні річка в нашому селі щороку виходить з берегів.
warmup.q: Every spring the river in our village ___.
warmup.explain: Річка виходить з берегів — the river bursts its banks.

A.q: The kids played football in the rain and came home ___ to the skin.
A.explain: Промокнути до нитки — get soaked to the skin. Watered — «политий» (про квіти), а wet як дієслово — «намочити».

A.q: The swallows are flying low, and it looks ___ rain.
A.explain: It looks like rain — схоже, буде дощ. Після like тут іменник rain.

A.q: We sat in the car for twenty minutes, waiting for the ___ rain to ease.
A.explain: Torrential rain — злива. Torrent — іменник (бурхливий потік), а strong із дощем зазвичай не кажуть.

B.q: It's calm now, but the wind will ___ up later this evening.
B.explain: The wind picks up — вітер посилюється. Протилежне — the wind dies down.

B.q: We drove at twenty miles an hour through the ___ fog.
B.explain: Густий туман — dense або thick fog. Strong fog — калька з «сильний туман».

B.q: The ___ wind made our eyes water as we waited for the ferry.
B.explain: Пронизливий, колючий вітер — a biting wind. Prickly — колючий на дотик (про кактус), bitten — «покусаний».

C.q: Last night's ___ winds blew our trampoline into the next garden.
C.explain: Gale-force winds — штормовий вітер. Gale-power і wind-force так не кажуть; ще сильніший вітер — storm-force або hurricane-force winds.

C.q: The town centre flooded when the river ___ its banks.
C.explain: Річка вийшла з берегів — the river burst its banks. Burst не змінюється: burst – burst – burst.

C.q: The hurricane ___ the island: hardly a building was left standing.

example.title: A camping weekend
example.uk:
У п'ятницю прогноз обіцяв суцільне сонце, тож ми поїхали з наметом до озера. Субота видалася пекельно спекотною, і ми цілий день лежали на траві й ніжилися на сонці.

У неділю зранку над пагорбами висіли густі хмари, і збиралося на дощ. До обіду вітер посилився, а незабаром полило як з відра. Ми промокли до нитки, поки знімали намет.

Дорогою додому через косий дощ було погано видно дорогу, а річечка поруч ледь не вийшла з берегів. Увечері, звісно ж, вітер ущух, і в хмарах з'явився просвіт. Як завжди!
example.en:
On Friday the forecast promised [[unbroken sunshine|a1]], so we drove to the lake with our tent. Saturday was [[scorching hot|a2]], and we lay on the grass all day, [[soaking up the sunshine|a3]].

On Sunday morning there was [[thick cloud|a10]] over the hills, and it [[looked like rain|a11]]. By lunchtime the wind had [[picked up|b16]], and soon it was [[pouring with rain|a4]]. We [[got soaked|a7]] while we were taking the tent down.

On the way home, the [[driving rain|b9]] made the road hard to see, and the little river next to it was close to [[bursting its banks|c9]]. In the evening, of course, the wind [[died down|b17]] and there was [[a break in the clouds|a8]]. Typical!
